subject: Energy
title: Thorium Reactors
description: A quick win: understand Thorium Reactors.

hook.text: Thorium is 3–4 times more abundant than uranium—and thorium reactors could produce far less long-lived waste.

buildup.text: Thorium can't sustain a chain reaction alone—it must be converted to uranium-233 inside the reactor first.

discovery.text: Molten salt reactors dissolve thorium fuel in liquid salt—operating at low pressure, eliminating explosion risks.

twist.text: India has the world's largest thorium reserves—and has pursued thorium reactors for decades, with limited success.

climax.text: China is building the first modern molten salt thorium reactor—expected to begin operations in the mid-2020s.

punchline.text: More abundant, less waste—thorium is nuclear's alternative path.

quiz.question: Why can't thorium sustain a chain reaction alone?
options: It must first be converted to uranium-233
